A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Oryx research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite the revised title, layout and numbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–E report original Oryx experiments, including T-Maze ablations, Connector and SMAX scaling, and SMAC, RWARE and MAMuJoCo benchmark results.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Section 4.4 adds an empirical comparison between Oryx and MAT+ICQ.

M1.justification: Oryx retains the same retention-based encoder, dual-output decoder, autoregressive ICQ updates, counterfactual advantage and Algorithm 1. MAT+ICQ is introduced as an experimental comparator; Oryx's procedure is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same T-Maze, Connector, SMAX, SMAC, RWARE and MAMuJoCo tasks and scenarios. The new architecture comparison reuses the existing SMAC and RWARE datasets.

E2.justification: Section 4.4 and Table 1 add MAT+ICQ, an offline MAT variant using Oryx's autoregressive ICQ loss, as a comparator on SMAC and RWARE. This is distinct from the existing MADT baseline. The earlier comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new architecture comparison specifies identical training procedures and the same ICQ loss, normalizes scores by each dataset's highest episode return, and aggregates median, IQM, mean and optimality gap across datasets. Existing experiments retain their evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds a focused backbone ablation comparing Sable-based Oryx with MAT under the same autoregressive ICQ objective across SMAC and RWARE. The earlier T-Maze component ablations and Connector/SMAX analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 introduces 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals for aggregate metrics. The existing seed counts, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and heteroscedastic two-sided t-tests are retained; no increase in existing experiments' run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds aggregate results favoring Oryx over MAT+ICQ: normalized IQM is 0.87 versus 0.67 on SMAC and 0.89 versus 0.85 on RWARE. These are newly reported comparisons. Previously reported benchmark values, T-Maze ablation results and scaling trends are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, advantage decomposition, Theorem 1, loss derivations, variance argument and Appendix A.1 proof are unchanged in substance. The proof's revised parentheses and spacing are typesetting changes.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the combination of Sable and autoregressive ICQ, effective many-agent coordination, and state-of-the-art performance on over 80% of 65 benchmark datasets. The revised title emphasizes sequence modeling without changing these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 interprets the new comparison as supporting the choice of Sable over MAT. The conclusion adds an outlook on extending autoregressive policies to other offline MARL methods and architectures. The existing limitation concerning real-world industrial applicability is retained.

D1.justification: V1 promises release of code, datasets and experimental data upon publication. V2 states that code and datasets are available and supplies a GitHub repository link in the introduction. Existing appendix implementation details and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Agarwal et al. (2021) and Gorsane et al. (2022) for statistical evaluation, and Fu et al. (2022) for the autoregressive-policy outlook. Section 4.4 sharpens the comparison with MAT. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged; bibliography reformatting and publication updates do not add distinct works.

P1.justification: V2 revises the title and author block, places the architecture explanation before the ICQ derivation, adds Section 4.4 and acknowledgments, and edits the introduction, conclusion and related-work ordering. Most existing prose and appendix content are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the architecture-comparison Table 1, relocates Figure 1, revises captions for Figures 2–4, adjusts several figure/table sizes and reformats the proof. The existing visual evidence is retained, with appendix tables renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new matched-objective MAT+ICQ comparison in Section 4.4 provides useful evidence for the Sable backbone choice that v1 lacked, with bootstrap intervals supporting the aggregate comparison. The stated code/data release and repository pointer also improve access information. These are focused gains in validation and reproducibility documentation; the method, proof and earlier benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
